title: Residential Natural Gas Supply Terms — Rollover at the End of a Term
content:
**Clause 1 — conversion.** When a Residential Natural Gas Supply term reaches its contract end date without a renewal election and without a pending cancellation, the agreement converts on the following day to the plan named as the rollover plan (Beacon Ridge Gas Monthly Variable), with a term of 0 months, no contract end date, and a plan change date set to the day after the expired contract end date.

**Clause 2 — rollover rate with compliant notices.** When both expiration notices were compliant, the rollover rate is the month-to-month rate stated in the final options notice.

**Clause 3 — late or missing notices.** When either notice was missing or not compliant, the expiring rate is held for the plan's late-notice hold period — 2 billing cycles on every plan — beginning with the first cycle after expiry, and the gas variable rate rules apply only after those cycles.

**Clause 4 — terms carried.** A rolled-over agreement carries the rollover plan's terms, including no early termination fee, and earns no sign-up credit.

### Rollover outcomes

| Both expiration notices compliant | Rate after expiry |
|---|---|
| Yes | the month-to-month rate stated in the final options notice |
| No (either missing or not compliant) | the expiring rate, held for 2 billing cycles from the first cycle after expiry; then the gas variable rate rules |

### Illustration (hypothetical dates)

A Beacon Ridge Gas Price Lock 12 term ends 31 May with no renewal election and no pending cancellation. On 1 June the agreement becomes Beacon Ridge Gas Monthly Variable, term 0 months, no contract end date, plan change date 1 June. If the initial renewal notice had been dated fewer than 45 days before 31 May, the expiring rate is held for the first 2 cycles after expiry.
